title: Certify exact dyadic root comparison with count surcharge
body:
Distinct dyadic profiles can have exactly equal roots under the actual count-dependent bit surcharge, leaving a safe interval comparison unresolved. This package completes PR1508's explicit surcharge-equality handoff: for m=2^k, dyadic ranks, positive integer stock and admitted nonnegative integer counts, it retains lambda=32m^2/10^16 and proves that the roots agree exactly when the monic polynomial GCD is negative at one. Otherwise rational brackets eventually separate. Counts and rank masses may differ.

The package includes direct-source-residual certificate checks independent of the primary polynomial compiler/GCD, unequal-count rational and irrational ties, a shared-negative-root counterexample, and a constant-GCD pair requiring 684 refinements. The unchanged pinned PR1392 signed-price routine is actually executed on both ties with assertions enabled, retaining its correct unresolved intervals. The polynomial GCD and bisection are standard techniques already present in PR1508; the new coverage is the actual surcharge contract and complete equality decision, not a claim that either predecessor is wrong.

Validation:

- Registered Python3.12.7 replay passes all 9,669 profile pairs, reverse checks, six named fixtures, 16 semantic controls and six end-to-end integrity tests.
- Optimized Python3.14.5 recomputes the identical complete receipt. A separate AI reviewer inspected the proof, source normalization and certificate logic, then independently passed the optimized Python3.12.14 replay.
- Source SHA256/Git blobs are checked before predecessor execution; Git-free export, altered executable source, typed/incomplete receipt and overwrite controls pass. Fresh main and predecessor heads remain unchanged; recent REST overlap supplements the older complete Discussion snapshot (GraphQL rate-limited).

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/surcharged-dyadic-comparator`.

Scope is arithmetic only. It does not integrate PR1392's fixed PR589 caller, whose idle rank42 is non-dyadic, or claim physical circuit realizability, supplier adoption, efficient worst-case separation, a complete invoice, selected cold replay or new kappa. Recursive hosting, precision/tape, bit H1-H5, hosted CI and independent human review remain unrun. The next question is a real caller whose entire profiles satisfy the exact branch's contract while preserving its replication/idle normalization.

Prepared by ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, verification and writing. Credit Hanson Sun (@bbMisk)/PR1508 for the unsurcharged comparator and explicit handoff; Brian Ross/PR1392 for retained-fee reference pricing; flemhhh/PR1048 for original interval routines; woklerx/PR1182 for endpoint repair; Douglas Colkitt for the existing fixed-exponent counterexample. Exact predecessor notices and licenses are retained. New work is Apache-2.0.
